releaseNotes:
### Added
- Compact, aligned configurator cards with complete firmware bindings, expandable
  explanations, safe network options and an optional authenticated web server.
- Per-entity Home Assistant exposure using compile-time `internal` substitutions.
  Hidden entities keep their firmware IDs, defaults and actions; diagnostics and
  recovery controls remain exposed by default.

### Changed
- Automatic timezone follows the browser on load and tab return, including saved
  and shared profiles. Disable Automatic timezone to keep an explicit manual zone.
- Installer, preview and saved/shared settings use one validated model for both
  ESP8266 and ESP-WROOM-32, without accepting or storing credentials.

groups.description: Identity and local time. Automatic timezone follows this browser, not the device location.
Clock face, time format and digit transitions. Preferences below are first-boot defaults; saved device preferences win after an update.

Choose any built-in screen. Automatic cycling alternates Clock and Date. Enter Home Assistant entity IDs at install time: this static configurator cannot query your entity list. Weather state provides the condition; a dedicated outdoor sensor is preferred, with the weather entity temperature attribute as fallback.
Brightness 0 is the dimmest MAX7219 level, not power off. Night scheduling follows the configured timezone; OTA and boot overlays stay visible.
Scroll speed is milliseconds per pixel: larger values are slower. A default duration of 0 keeps a message until cleared. Preview text is not installed.
Rebuild after changing wiring or board. Modules must divide evenly into rows. Selecting 180° also reverses the chip chain; change the chain switch separately for unusual wiring.

Non-secret options only. SSID and credentials stay in your local secret file. A timeout of 0 disables that automatic reboot or fallback-hotspot timer; this can make recovery harder. Keep the default SNTP interval unless your time server permits more frequent polling.

Optional authenticated device page. Disable it to save flash; native API and encrypted OTA remain available, but the fallback hotspot then has no browser page. Hidden entities stay hidden here too. Web OTA and internal-entity listing remain disabled. HTTP is unencrypted with either authentication method: use a trusted LAN. Digest avoids sending the password directly. Web UI version 1 is deprecated by ESPHome.
Firmware timing, logs and OTA. A longer redraw interval reduces update frequency and can make animation less smooth. Firmware compilation, flash size and on-device behavior remain unverified.
